text:
**Short answer:** Get a LiFePO4 station of about 1 kWh or more with at least 600 W of AC output. My top pick is the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2.

**Why a pellet smoker is easy to power:** A pellet grill draws little once it's lit. The auger, fan and controller use about 35–60 W. Only the igniter pulls 200–400 W, and only for the first few minutes ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight)). One measured run, a Z Grills on a Jackery Explorer 1000, used just 210 Wh in 6 hours. A full overnight cook comes to roughly 450–750 Wh, according to the same source. [Volt & Valley](https://voltandvalley.com/tailgate-travel/best-power-station-for-a-pellet-grill) says a 1,024 Wh unit covers a full overnight cook. Its figure is about 16 hours at a 50 W draw.

BLUETTI's own guide assumes a higher average draw of 150–250 W ([BLUETTI](https://www.bluettipower.com/blogs/buying-guide/how-long-can-bluetti-power-pellet-grill-smoker)). So check your grill's label and test it with a watt meter. A cold-weather or high-temperature cook will use more than a low-and-slow one.

**Picks:**
- **Best overall: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 ($899).**
  - It has 2,073.6 Wh and a 2,600 W inverter, which easily handles the igniter.
  - Dealectric says it covers two or three 12-hour cooks, and it was in stock as of 2026-11-04.
  - [Buy here](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2). Dealectric says the link pre-applies code DEALECTRIC for $44.95 off. Dealectric sells it, and the page isn't independent.
- **Cheaper, one night: BLUETTI AC180 (1,152 Wh, 1,800 W, $449).** It's enough for one overnight cook, but Dealectric says it's back in stock in late November ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight)).
- **Also fits one night: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (1,070 Wh, 1,500 W).** It's the same class as the unit in the measured Z Grills run. Dealectric lists no price, so check Amazon.
- **Short cooks or a tight budget: BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 (288 Wh, 600 W, $289.99).** It gives about 5 hours for a 35 W smoker, so it won't cover an overnight cook.

**Watch the surge rating:** The igniter is what trips small units. Volt & Valley warns that a 300 W continuous / 600 W surge inverter is marginal against a 350–500 W igniter. It recommends a 600 W unit with a 1,500 W surge over a weaker one.

**What to skip:**
- **Grilla Power Station ($359.99):** It claims a 10-hour runtime with 300 W output ([Grilla](https://www.grillagrills.com/product/1197809)). That's the marginal output class, so confirm it works with your grill's igniter.
- **Results on "electric smokers":** The [HomePowerFacts](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-smoker/) page assumes about 1,000 W of continuous draw, which is a different appliance. Its "none lasts 8 hours" conclusion doesn't apply to a pellet smoker.

**Campsite tips:** Keep the battery dry and away from heat, grease, ash and foot traffic. Run a full startup-to-shutdown test at home first. Phones and lights on the same battery cut your runtime ([GearBrain video summary](https://open.video/%40gearbrain/v/can-a-portable-power-station-run-a-pellet-grill)).
